Combine several independent p-values per feature into one, by Fisher's or Stouffer's method

stats_combine_p.Rd

Combine several independent p-values for each feature into one, by Fisher's or Stouffer's method, optionally weighted and optionally signed by each test's effect.

Each feature is combined on its own by mzLib's PValueCombination: Fisher (1925), X = -2 sum ln p against chi-square on 2k degrees of freedom, or Stouffer (1949), Z = sum w z / sqrt(sum w^2) against the standard normal. mzLib holds both to R's pchisq() and qnorm() to 1e-8 relative. Use it when you have one p-value per study - per dataset, cohort or laboratory - for the same feature, and want one answer from all of them.

Usage

stats_combine_p(tests, method, timeout = 60)

Arguments

tests

A data.frame with one row per test: feature and p_value, and optionally weight and effect columns. A feature's tests need not be adjacent. p_value is a fraction from 0 to 1, or NA for a test that could not be run (it is omitted, and counted in the omitted column). weight (Stouffer only) is a positive number, for example the square root of the study's sample size; give it for every test or for none (NA is no weight). effect is the test's estimate in any unit; give it for every test or for none, and NA for a test with no direction (omitted). An effect column without a weight column sends no weights.

method

"fisher" or "stouffer". Required: mzLib has no preferred rule. Fisher is driven by the strongest single result and takes no weights; Stouffer weighs every study, and takes weights.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

Direction. Both rules combine *one-sided* p-values. A two-sided p-value from stats_fit does not say which way the effect went, so two studies that disagree look like two that agree. Give every test its effect (its estimate; only the sign is used) and mzLib first turns each p into the one-sided p-value for effect > 0 (PValueCombination.OneSided: p/2 for a positive effect, 1 - p/2 for a negative one), so opposite effects cancel. The combined p_value then tests effect > 0; for Stouffer, a p_value near 1 means a consistently negative effect.

Neither rule estimates an effect size: stats_meta does that, from estimates and standard errors. Neither adjusts across features: send records$p_value to stats_adjust.

Value

An mzlibr_combined_p_values:

- records, a data.frame with one row per feature in order of first appearance: feature; studies, the tests combined (tests with a finite p-value, after the signed conversion when effects were given); omitted, the feature's tests that were not combined (tests): no p-value, or (signed) an effect of 0 or NA; statistic, Fisher's X or Stouffer's Z (fisher: chi-square statistic on 2 x studies degrees of freedom; stouffer: standard normal deviates), NA when it is not finite; and p_value, a fraction (0 to 1), the upper tail of the statistic, so ONE direction (effect > 0 when signed), NA when there is nothing to combine, or a p of 0 and a p of 1 together (Stouffer). An NA statistic with a p-value is an infinite one: p_value 0 means plus infinity (a p-value of 0 among the tests), 1 means minus infinity (Stouffer, a p-value of 1). - method, as you asked; weighted (Stouffer with weights); signed (effects were given, so every p-value was read as two-sided and converted before combining); line_count tests (lines) sent over every feature; feature_count features; row_count rows; column_names. - caveats: what the combination assumes, plus any that apply to this input (omitted tests, infinite statistics).

The trap

Two-sided p-values given without their effects are combined as if one-sided, so two studies whose effects point opposite ways reinforce each other instead of cancelling. Give effect for that. mzLib computes no two-sided combined p-value.

Wraps

Wire verb stats combine-p. Generated from the bridge's verb spec stats.combine-p.yaml (bridge commit 84c3b984b6b9) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • PValueCombination.Stouffer in mzLib/StatisticalModels/PValueCombination.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • CombinedPValue in mzLib/StatisticalModels/PValueCombination.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

method

string; required; range fisher | stouffer. The combination rule. REQUIRED: mzLib has the two as separate methods and prefers neither, so the bridge picks none. fisher is PValueCombination.Fisher, Fisher (1925): X = -2 sum ln p, referred to chi-square with 2k degrees of freedom; it is driven by the smallest p-values and takes no weights. stouffer is PValueCombination.Stouffer, Stouffer et al. (1949): Z = sum w z / sqrt(sum w^2) with z = the standard normal quantile of 1 - p, referred to N(0, 1); it weighs every test.

tests (wire --stdin)

string[]; required; range >= 1 line of 2 to 4 tab-separated fields. One test per line, tab-separated: feature, p_value, then optionally weight and effect. No header; blank lines are skipped; a UTF-8 BOM is dropped. A feature's lines need not be adjacent: features are reported in order of first appearance, and each is combined by its own mzLib call. p_value is a fraction in [0, 1]; a blank, NA or NaN p_value is a test that could not be run, which mzLib omits. weight (stouffer only; a positive number, for example the square root of the study's sample size) must be on every line or on none; a blank or NA third field is no weight. effect (the test's estimate, any unit: only its sign is used) must be a fourth field on every line or on none. With effects, each p_value is read as TWO-SIDED and converted by PValueCombination.OneSided to the one-sided p-value for effect > 0 (p/2 for a positive effect, 1 - p/2 for a negative one) before combining; an effect that is 0, blank, NA or NaN has no direction, so mzLib returns NaN and the test is omitted. Write feature, p, a blank weight and the effect to give an effect without a weight.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

method

string; never NA. fisher | stouffer, as given.

weighted

bool; never NA. Whether the lines carried weights (stouffer only).

signed

bool; never NA. Whether the lines carried effects, so each p-value was read as two-sided and converted to the one-sided p-value for effect > 0.

line_count

int; in lines; never NA. Test lines read from stdin, over every feature.

feature_count

int; in features; never NA. Distinct features; the table's row count.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. Equal to feature_count.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns, in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per feature, in order of first appearance.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Three static caveats, plus: two when signed (one only for fisher), and one each when any test was omitted (with the count), when a feature has nothing left to combine, when a feature holds both a p-value of 0 and of 1 (stouffer), and when a statistic is infinite.

Columns of records

feature

string; never NA. As given on stdin.

studies

int; in tests; never NA. Tests combined: mzLib's CombinedPValue.Studies, the finite p-values after any signed conversion.

omitted

int; in tests; never NA. This feature's lines that were not combined: a blank, NA or NaN p_value, or (signed) an effect that is 0, blank, NA or NaN. studies + omitted is the feature's line count.

statistic

float; in fisher: chi-square statistic on 2 x studies degrees of freedom; stouffer: standard normal deviates; NA when not finite. With studies 0, nothing was combined (p_value null too). Otherwise p_value says which: 0 means plus infinity (a p-value of 0 among the tests), 1 means minus infinity (stouffer, a p-value of 1), and null means undefined (stouffer, a p-value of 0 and one of 1 together). Fisher's X = -2 sum ln p, or Stouffer's Z = sum w z / sqrt(sum w^2).

p_value

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when studies is 0 (nothing to combine), or stouffer met a p-value of 0 and one of 1 (z of plus and minus infinity). Combined p-value: the UPPER tail of the statistic's reference distribution, so it tests one direction (effect > 0 when signed). Fisher's is the regularized upper incomplete gamma Q(k, X/2), so a tiny value keeps its digits. Not adjusted across features.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--method missing, given without a value, or not fisher or stouffer; stdin empty; a line with fewer than 2 or more than 4 tab-separated fields; an empty feature name; a p_value, weight or effect that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN)

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

a weight on some lines and not others; an effect field on some lines and not others; any weight with --method fisher

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses a feature's input, named in the message: a p-value outside [0, 1], or a weight that is not finite and positive (mzLib's ArgumentException, reclassified)

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • Both rules assume the tests are independent and test the same one-sided hypothesis. Fisher is driven by the smallest p-values; Stouffer weighs every test, and with weights (for example the square root of each study's sample size) lets larger studies count more.

  • p_value is the upper tail of the statistic, so it tests one direction. Two-sided p-values given without their effects are combined as if one-sided, and opposite effects then reinforce each other instead of cancelling: give each test's effect for that.

  • Neither rule estimates an effect size; pool the estimates with stats meta for that. p_value is not adjusted across features; send the p_value column to stats adjust.

  • Signed: p_value tests effect > 0, and for stouffer a p_value near 1 means a consistently negative effect. mzLib computes no two-sided combined p-value. For a negative effect whose two-sided p-value is below about 2e-16, 1 - p/2 rounds to 1, so that test's z is minus infinity and decides a stouffer feature (p_value 1).

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Examples


# mzLib's own reference cases (constructed p-values, not proteomics data), by both rules:
cases <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "stats", "combination_inputs.tsv", package = "mzLibR"))
fisher <- stats_combine_p(data.frame(feature = cases$case, p_value = cases$p), method = "fisher")
stouffer <- stats_combine_p(data.frame(feature = cases$case, p_value = cases$p,
  weight = cases$weight), method = "stouffer")
data.frame(feature = fisher$records$feature, studies = fisher$records$studies,
  fisher = signif(fisher$records$p_value, 3),
  weighted_stouffer = signif(stouffer$records$p_value, 3))
#>   feature studies   fisher weighted_stouffer
#> 1     few       3 8.71e-02          0.150000
#> 2    tiny       4 3.14e-11          0.002280
#> 3     one       1 3.70e-02          0.037000
#> 4    many      12 1.13e-01          0.032300
#> 5   mixed       5 1.91e-02          0.713000
#> 6    tail       3 2.14e-18          0.000836
